videos.title: 诺和诺德黄金时代结束？我继续加仓|  NVO  | Novo Nordisk  | Wegovy | 礼来 |  LLY
videos.transcript: By the close of business Monday, Novo  Nordisk had seen another 800 billion  Danish krone in market value evaporate.  More bizarrely, on the same day, Novo  Nordisk announced that its new drug had  beaten Eli Lilly's flagship product in  a head-to-head trial, yet the stock  didn't rally—it plummeted 8%in a  single day. Novo Nordisk, the company  that once revolutionized the global  weight-loss market with a single pen,  is now facing a much more brutal stress  test. In today’s video, I’ll break  down the key news from Novo Nordisk’s  Capital Markets Day last week. What is  the real reason behind the stock's  recent avalanche? And what is my  assessment of the company’s latest  investment value? Hi everyone, this is  US Stock Doctor, sharing essential US  market insights every week. This is my  core analysis, so be sure to watch  until the end. I’ve divided today's  video into three parts: first, the  major signals from Novo Nordisk's  Capital Markets Day; second, why the  market didn't give a positive reaction;  and third, my perspective on Novo  Nordisk's investment value. First,  let’s go back to September 21st, this  past Monday. Novo Nordisk held its  highly anticipated Capital Markets Day  in London, the first time new CEO Lars  Fruergaard Jørgensen fully outlined  the company's future strategic  blueprint to global investors.  Logically, this should have been an  event to boost confidence, with the CEO  presenting a seemingly stellar  scorecard, promising to launch five  blockbuster new drugs by 2030. By 2035,  the company aims for over $ 23 billion  in new pipeline sales, with Phase 3  clinical data for their core  experimental drug, CagriSema, showing  an average weight reduction of 12.4%,  outperforming their own Wegovy's 9.1%.  If you look at the data alone, you  might think this was a textbook " king’s return," but in reality, on  the day the conference concluded, Novo  Nordisk's US ADR closed down 8%,  falling nearly 9%at one point, while  European shares also dropped over 7%,  making it one of the day’s  worst-performing large caps. However,  that was just the beginning; the next  day, the stock didn't bounce back but  continued to slide, falling another 3% by Wednesday. In just a few trading  days, Novo Nordisk’s market value has  evaporated by over $ 60 billion. So the  question is: since Novo Nordisk  announced positive clinical data for  its next-gen weight-loss drug, why has  its stock price continued to plummet?  Now let's move on to the second part:  what exactly disappointed the market  about this company? To answer this  clearly, we first need to understand  why the market previously gave Novo  Nordisk such a high valuation. Because  it wasn't just a big pharma company; it  was a money-printing machine that  achieved explosive growth far above the  industry average, fueled by two  semaglutide-based products: Ozempic and  Wegovy. This logic once propelled its  market value to the trillion Danish  krone level. However, at this Capital  Markets Day, management admitted that  Novo Nordisk's growth rate will  gradually return to the industry  average over the next five years. This  is effectively telling the market to  reprice Novo Nordisk as an ordinary  pharmaceutical stock rather than using  a hyper-growth valuation model. This is  the part that bothers professional  investors the most, as a shift in  valuation framework has far more  profound and lasting consequences than  fluctuations in clinical data for a  single drug. In other words, the change  in the management's growth model is the  root cause of this slump, and the  market is systematically re-evaluating  whether Novo Nordisk deserves its  former star-stock valuation. Of course,  if it were just slow growth, the market  could accept it to some extent, because  a major pharmaceutical company will  always have another blockbuster product  in its R&D pipeline. But the current  problem with Novo Nordisk is that it is  unclear if its next-generation  weight-loss products can keep the  momentum going. Next, I will explain  something that many other creators  haven't clarified. First: the real  reason why the CagriSema trial  succeeded but the market isn't buying  it. In a show over half a year ago, I  mentioned a trial that caused Novo  Nordisk's stock to plummet: the OASIS 1  trial. In this trial, Novo Nordisk  pitted its 2.4 mg CagriSema against Eli  Lilly’s 15mg tirzepatide in an 84- week open-label head-to-head study. The  result? CagriSema achieved 23%weight  loss—a decent number, but the  competitor’s tirzepatide reached 25.5 %. Novo Nordisk failed to prove it was  not inferior to its rival, meaning the  Novo Nordisk product didn't perform  much differently from the competitor's  drug. Please note, "failing to prove  better" and "proving worse" are both  inaccurate descriptions here. How heavy  is the frustration from this trial  failure? Novo Nordisk spent hundreds of  millions of dollars and recruited over  800 patients for this trial just to  prove CagriSema could win, only to end  up with an embarrassing official report . Novo Nordisk lost, which can be  interpreted as a clear defeat by a  competitor in a ring of their own  design. Fast-forward to this  September's Capital Markets Day, where  Novo Nordisk presented the latest  clinical trial data for CagriSema. In  this study, the low-dose CagriSema  group achieved a 12.4%weight loss,  outperforming the 9.1%seen in the  tirzepatide group. At first glance,  this looks like a revenge match, but if  you compare these two trials  side-by-side, you will spot the problem . First, the trial populations have  changed: Redefine 4 focused on obesity  or overweight individuals, while  Reimagine 5 focused on patients with  type 2 diabetes and comorbidities. In  other words, the patient population in  Reimagine 5 is completely different  from that of Redefine 4. Well, type 2  diabetes itself is a significant  clinical factor affecting weight loss  results, so the absolute weight loss  figures from these two trials cannot be  directly compared. Second, and more  importantly, the dosage has changed.  This time, the control group wasn't the  15mg high dose of tirzepatide, but 5mg,  which is a noticeably conservative  low-to-mid dose. CagriSema was also  used at 1.0 mg, not its highest dosage  either. Why not choose the highest  approved dosage? Because Novo Nordisk's  management stated that not all patients  are suited for the highest dosage.  Therefore, this Reimagine 5 trial and  the previous Redefine 4 are not the  same competition; the patient  populations are different, the dosages  are different, and the experimental  goals are different. So, the 12.4% versus 9.1%gap cannot be directly  interpreted as CagriSema having  surpassed Zepbound in weight loss  efficacy. The market's interpretation  was straightforward: this wasn't a fair  revenge match, but a carefully  orchestrated "victory." By avoiding its  own biggest weaknesses and dodging the  rival's strongest firepower, they  produced results that look impressive  but are questionable in substance. A  more realistic issue is that even if  not all patients need the highest dose,  what the market—and investors who  value these drugs—cares about most  remains the absolute efficacy of the  drug in weight reduction. This is the  battlefield where Novo Nordisk's  semaglutide and Eli Lilly's tirzepatide  are going head-to-head. Even though the  results of Novo's Reimagine 5 trial are  positive, the market isn't fully buying  it, because the numbers don't answer  the real, lingering question: at the  highest dose, is Novo Nordisk's  next-gen CagriSema actually effective?  Given these two reasons—first, that  Novo Nordisk's growth is about to slow  down, and second, that this latest  head-to-head trial lacks sufficient  substance—it explains why, despite  Novo Nordisk releasing what seemed to  be good news, the market remains  skeptical. After covering the latest  Capital Markets Day updates, we move to  the third part: the investment value of  Novo Nordisk. To clarify this, I’d  like to break it down into three layers . First, how is the company’s  business actually performing right now?  Currently, the company’s Wegovy, with  semaglutide as its core component,  remains the primary cash cow of the GLP -1 sector. Although price wars in the  US market are intensifying, Novo has  reached an agreement with the Trump  administration to significantly lower  the out-of-pocket monthly costs for  semaglutide. While this compresses  profit margins in the short term, it  secures a stance of legal and compliant  proactive price reduction, which to  some extent silences public criticism.  On the other side, thanks to the strong  performance of Zepbound, based on  tirzepatide, Lilly continues to expand  its market share. But note this: the  battle for market share is essentially  about production capacity and  distribution, no longer just pure  efficacy dominance. With both companies  'core products proving effective, the  next phase is a competition over who  can deliver drugs to patients faster  and more affordably. The second layer  is: where are the new growth points?  Novo Nordisk’s first card is the  commercial prospect of CagriSema. Based  on data from the REDEFINE 1 and 2 Phase  3 clinical trials, Novo Nordisk  submitted a New Drug Application for  weight management last December. The  FDA is expected to provide a decision  in Q4 this year, and the company plans  to launch in early 2027. In other words , the market's concern about CagriSema  potentially falling short against  competitors will soon be addressed.  However, please note that "falling  short" here refers to the maximum  effect at the highest dosage, not that  the drug lacks commercial value. The  second card is the oral version of  semaglutide. It is the world’s first  oral GLP-1 drug approved for adult  weight loss. Although Lilly's oral  weight-loss drug hit the US market this  April, its uptake speed is  significantly lower than that of oral  semaglutide during the same period.  Moreover, based on current  cross-comparisons of public clinical  data, oral semaglutide maintains a  relative lead in weight-loss efficacy.  Combined with Novo Nordisk’s  one-quarter head start in the market,  this first-mover advantage remains a  protective moat for the company in the  short term. The third card is the  series of follow-up pipelines announced  at the Capital Markets Day, from the  high-dose version of CagriSema to  monotherapy, and then to the  longer-term Amycretin. Novo Nordisk has  shown they are playing a comprehensive  game of multi-generational product  relay, rather than betting everything  on a single drug. This means that even  if CagriSema fails to become a  blockbuster, this company still has  more than one card to play. Finally,  the last layer is how I interpret the  investment value of Novo Nordisk. I  have already made many episodes about  this company. Over the past year or so,  its stock price has fallen by 40%. The  market has basically priced in all the  bad news imaginable, such as slowing  growth, disappointing data for some  drugs, pricing pressure in the US,  patent cliffs, and intensified  competition—all these factors are  reflected in the current stock price.  So, the risks I am willing to take  include competitors continuing to grab  market share, CagriSema’s  commercialization falling short of  expectations, the patent expiration of  Semaglutide in some regions, and future  growth falling below previous levels.  The returns I believe I might get  include continued volume growth for  current drugs, decent sales performance  for their products, the success of Novo  Nordisk's next-generation pipeline, and  the continued expansion of the overall  GLP-1 market size. Therefore, my  current position building is not  because Novo Nordisk has eliminated all  risks, but because I believe the risks  facing this company are relatively  clear. Considering that I am very  bullish on the GLP-1 track, I am  personally willing to take on these  risks by building my position in  batches, continuously buying as the  stock price remains between $ 35 and $  40. If the stock price continues to  fall by 10%, I will continue to buy  more. Of course, this is just my  personal analytical logic and  investment decision; after all,  certainty never exists in the market.  Furthermore, I already hold some Novo  Nordisk shares, so some of my views  above may be colored by bias. Therefore , you can treat this episode as me  providing a very subjective and skewed  perspective to assist you in  understanding the investment value of  Novo Nordisk. However, you still need  to combine your own risk appetite with  other perspectives to make  comprehensive judgments and reach your  own independent investment decisions.  Alright, that is my latest assessment  of the investment value of Novo Nordisk . Next, we move on to the portfolio  disclosure. Hello everyone, my return  rate for this week is 4.97%. Since  March 2022, the total account return  rate is 24.61%. This week, I bought 150  shares of Novo Nordisk at $ 39.51, and  I also continued my weekly $ 500  investment in Microsoft; there were no  other changes. In this segment today,  I'd like to discuss the multinational  giant Novartis, with the stock ticker  NVS. This very stable European  pharmaceutical company recently saw its  stock price collapse. On September 4th,  just four days after Novartis announced  a major Phase 3 cardiovascular trial,  another Phase 3 trial for a  neuromuscular disease ended in failure.  The result was that on September 8th,  Novartis plunged 14%in a single day,  marking one of its worst trading days  in history, as the stock price fell  from around $ 160 to $ 137. Regarding  this company, what I'm focused on isn't  just the failure of these two drugs,  but why the market reacted so strongly  to these two failures. Because  investors have perhaps started to doubt  not just one specific drug, but whether  Novartis's pipeline for the coming  years is actually strong enough.  Looking at the first one, this is a  cholesterol-lowering drug that Novartis  has been betting on for many years. The  protein this drug targets affects about  one in five people globally, and there  is currently no approved targeted  therapy, so high hopes were placed on  this drug; however, the Phase 3  clinical results released on September  4th showed that while the drug had an  effect on the target, it failed to  prove it could significantly reduce the  risk of cardiovascular events,  ultimately missing its primary endpoint . This was already disappointing enough  for investors, but more trouble  followed when, a few days later,  Novartis announced more bad news: an  innovative drug for muscular dystrophy  had failed. It came from a $ 12 billion  acquisition Novartis just completed  this year; Novartis spent so much money  hoping to gain a next-generation RNA  therapy platform and several products  in late-stage development from this  company. But on September 8th, the  Phase 3 clinical trial results for this  drug also failed to reach its endpoints . This is interesting: one was a  blockbuster drug Novartis had bet on  for a long time, and the other was a " future" Novartis bought for $ 12  billion. With two projects running into  problems within a few days, the market  naturally began to ask a bigger  question: whether Novartis's growth  model of using R&D plus acquisitions to  continuously seek the next blockbuster  drug can still function. And it didn't  end there; on September 16th, Novartis  decided to terminate a drug called  VHB937, which targeted epilepsy,  because its mid-stage clinical trial  failed to meet its primary and  secondary endpoints. In other words, in  just two short weeks, the market  witnessed three consecutive R&D  failures, which is why the stock price  plummeted. However, as one of the  world's most stable pharmaceutical  giants, Novartis saw its Q2 sales grow  by 1%at constant currencies. Core  products maintained solid growth, and  the company did not lower its full-year  guidance, expecting single-digit growth  in sales through 2026. This isn't a  company suddenly devoid of revenue or  profit; what has truly changed is the  market's confidence in its future  growth. Novartis previously set a sales  growth target of 5%to 6%for 2025 to  2030, while relying on substantial R&D  and external acquisitions to fill  future product gaps. The company stated  last year that it expected over 15 key  clinical readouts that could support  filings within two years. But now,  several projects that were supposed to  help open up its future potential have  encountered successive problems.  However, if we look at the company's  stock price, it hasn't crashed like  some other star stocks, because this  company is steady and conservative. If  you like this type of company, you  might want to keep an eye on Novartis.  Anyway, I personally feel that if you  compare Novo Nordisk and Novartis, I  still find Novo Nordisk to have more  room for imagination. By the way,  I’ve started a fitness account called  "Bu Duo Chi Yi Kou," which I update on  Xiaohongshu and Douyin. You are all  welcome to follow. And most importantly , if you found this video even slightly  insightful, I would really, really  appreciate it if you could click the  account opening link pinned in the  comments section—just click it and  then close it. Clicking it won't cost  you a penny, but it’s like buying me  a cup of coffee. It is the most  important way to support my channel's  updates. Thank you very much. Alright,  that’s all for today’s video. See  you in the next one.

videos.title: Covered Call 备兑开仓｜股票如何“收租”？收益、风险与行权价选择
videos.transcript: 你有一套房子 市场价呢 300个w 你住了5年 你面前呢 有两个选择 第一个继续住着它 等着它慢慢涨 第二个一边住一边呢 把空余的房间收租金 每个月多拿8,000块 聪明的人呢 会选第二个 期权市场里的covered call的策略 其实做的就是这件事 你手里持有的股票就是你的房子 权利金就是你每月收到的租金 很多人做期权上来就想 买call买put是吧 我要博弈方向 我做了12年期权 我想告诉你 最稳健的一个策略 往往是那个最无聊的 今天这个视频呢 我把covered call彻底给你讲明白 看完之后你会发现 这简直是给上班族量身定做的策略 先搞清楚covered call到底是什么 covered call中文名叫备兑开仓 听起来很专业是吧 逻辑特别简单 你持有100股某只股票 同时卖出一张这只股票的call期权 就这么简单 备兑的意思是什么 意思是你已经持有100股 备着然后兑出去 卖出看涨期权 收到一笔权利金 美国市场期权合约一张 对应100股的现货 这是基本的规则 这里面有一个概念啊 CBOE，芝加哥商品期权交易所 一个硬核的数据啊 我给你分享一下 这边呢是一个指数叫BXM指数 从1986年开始追踪标普500 的covered call策略的表现 将近40年真实的数据啊 covered call策略的年化收益率能达到9.8% 纯持有标普500是10.9% 看着少赚了一个点 但是波动率比标普500跌了26% 换算成夏普比率 也就是每承担一份风险 换来的回报 covered call反而更优 我们翻译一下 你少赚一点点 但是你睡觉睡得更踏实了 对于不想天天盯盘的上班族 很划算啊 我们用数字说话 一个完整的例子 如果说你150美元买入100股苹果的股票 总投入15,000美元 现价是150美元 你卖出一个一个月后 到期的行权价165美金的call 收取权利金是3美元每股 也就是300美元 这300美元立刻进入到你的账户啊 不管一个月股价怎么走 这个钱都是你的 一个月之后会出现两种情况 第一种情况是什么 苹果的股价涨到165以上 比如说170美元 你的股票被行权 你以165元卖出 你的股票收益什么 165-150乘以100是1500美元 权利金收入是300美元 总收益是1,800美元 持仓收益率12% 你的股票呢 从150涨到170 你赚了1,500美元 还额外拿了300的权利金 这就是covered call的魅力啊 涨了你也赚 只是170以上的部分被截断了 但是你多了一笔稳稳的租金 第二种苹果股价没有到165 比如还在155 买方不行权 你的股票呢继续持有 权利金300美金照收不误 股票呢比如说浮盈可能是500美元 你的权利金呢是300美元收入 总账面收益是800美元 更为关键的是什么 你下个月可以再卖一次covered call策略 再收一次权利金 这就是为什么covered call像收房租 你每个月呢都可以收一次 为什么我说这是最适合上班族的策略呢 有三个原因 第一个你不需要盯盘对吧 你持有的股票再加上卖出的call 就是一个收租型的组合 你不需要每天看盘 猜数据看涨跌 只要股票的基本面没问题 你每月的收租就行了 上班的人没法盯盘 这简直是一个完美的策略 第二个你有了一个安全垫 收了权利金相当于什么 降低了你的持仓成本 你以150块钱买的股票 收了3块钱权利金 实际的持仓成本是147 股价跌一点你也不慌 因为你有一个缓冲带 第三很重要啊 胜率极高 CBOE有一个数据统计 covered call的策略在 标普500上的胜率大概是88.9% 即便个股分散持仓 成功率是在82%左右 也就是做10次 你有8次左右是盈利的 这在期权里面属于 非常高的一种确定性了 说到covered call的最常见的误区 我给你讲一个真实的案例 我有一个朋友 圈里人管他叫满上哥 策略只有一个叫满仓干 他学了covered call的策略让我差点喷出来 就是把所有的资金全仓买 了一个生物医药的公司 美国的一个股票 然后卖出4张covered call 我问他你为什么不分散一下他说 一只股票打透效率最高 covered call的精髓是什么 我本来持有这个股票 顺便收一点点租金是吧 但是你现在把鸡蛋都放在一个篮子里 那不叫covered call 那叫什么 集中持仓加卖看涨期权 风险完全不一样 后来那家公司发了什么临床数据 股价跳空涨了30%啊 他的4张call全部被行权了 被call走了 账面上确实赚了一笔 但是那30%的涨幅被行权价截断了 他少赚了一些利润 我说万一临床数据如果不及预期呢 如果它跌40%你怎么办 他想了一想 他说哦 那确实问题很大 这非常像一个人把全部的积蓄拿去了 买入了一个巨额的意外险 你觉得他是做财务规划 实际上他是把身家 押注在一件不发生的事 covered call是分散持仓、稳健收租 不是把鸡蛋放在一个篮子里 然后美其名曰我在收租 正确的做法是什么 分散持仓啊 比如说你单只股票的covered call仓位 不超过你总体头寸的20%或者30% 留出足够的现金做缓冲 任何策略都有弱点 covered call的最大弱点是什么 两个字踏空 我们回到刚才那个例子啊 苹果股票150块买入 卖了一个165的call 收了3块钱权利金 苹果的财报如果超预期 股价直接涨（口误）到200美元 你的股票被行权 你以165去卖出了 你赚了1,800美元，1,500+300 但如果你只有持有股票能赚5,000美元 你为了300（口误）美元的权利金 损失了将近3,200的额外收入 这就是covered call的代价 你卖掉了什么 上涨的潜力 换来了确定性的收入 CBOE的数据更直接啊 牛市的年份 标普500平均涨22% covered call策略的收益只有15% 平均少赚了7个百分点 过去的十年 BXM这个指数只捕获了 标普500上涨收益的63% 却承受了88%的下跌幅度 这就像你请了一个管家帮你去看房子 管家每个月交你一笔租金 但是房价暴涨的时候 他有权按照约定的价格把房子买走 你收了租金 但是丢了涨幅 covered call有一个明确的禁区 当股票发财报或者重大的利好 处于一个明显的主升浪行情时候 不要卖call啊 那时候上涨的空间是巨大的 你会截断 让你非常的难受 反过来说 CBOE的数据显示 在震荡时 covered call每年跑赢标普500有5个百分点 这是它的主战场 行权价的选择怎么选呢 30年数据回测给出你的答案 很多新手纠结行权价选多高啊 CBOE对标普500做了30年的回测 对比了三个维度 给你做一个参考 第一个叫Delta 20 年化权利金约3.5% 行权概率18% 上涨捕获率88% 年化回报呢 11.8% Delta30 权利金约5.2% 年化回报约12.4% 夏普比率呢 0.65 Delta40呢年化权利金呢约7% 被行权概率提高了 上涨捕获率63% 年化回报11% 所以说Delta 30是一个 公认的这么一个甜蜜点 他选的一个大概率涨不到 但是也不可能涨到这么一个仓位 权利金不会太少 但是被行权的概率也不会特别高啊 具体操作我们要看两个核心的指标 第一个叫时间 选择30天到45天的合约 这个时间段的时间衰减最快 对你很有利啊 第二，IV（隐含波动率） 如果说高IV的时候你卖call 的权利金赚得更多 数据回测也显示了 CBOE IV在70以上卖covered call 每个周期比IV低的时候多赚2.3% 我做过一笔印象特别深刻的covered call 2022年美股呢有一个大跌 我在一批优质的标的上卖covered call 当时市场很恐慌啊 IV特别高 权利金也非常的厚 有一笔交易我记得非常清楚 买入价格65美元 卖出行权价什么呢 75美元的call 一个月收租4.5美元的 这个每股的这种权利金 相当于持股成本的7% 一个月7%的收益啊 我觉得很好啊 后来那个股价在68-72之间完成震荡 没有达到75 权利金全部收到了 下个月继续卖 这就是covered call在震荡市里面特别舒服 股票不涨也不跌 安安稳稳的去收权利金 这就特别像一段特别好的婚姻关系 不需要大起大落的激情 平稳运转本身就是最大的收益 covered call就是让你的持仓月月收房租 觉得有用点个赞关注我

videos.title: Is AI a bubble?  #nvidia #stockmarket #stocks
videos.transcript: Nvidia is guaranteeing up to $105 billion of OpenAI's data center lease. OpenAI promises $300 billion to Oracle. And Oracle spends about $40 billion buying Nvidia's chips. It's essentially the same money just going in a circle. And it looks exactly like a bubble. And yes, you should care because these are the biggest names within your index fund. We've seen this circle before. In the year 2000, Cisco lent telecom startups the money to buy Cisco's own equipment. Cambrian Communications borrowed about $70 million from Cisco to buy Cisco's gear. And when it went bankrupt, it listed assets under about $50,000, which is about the same price of a new car. And frankly, Cambrian wasn't a one-off. It was one of 47 telecoms that collapsed the same way in just 3 years. And in return, Cisco got absolutely crushed because $10,000 in its stock quickly became just 1,000. and it didn't climb back up to its original $10,000 until December 2025. That's 25 years where the stock was completely underwater. But today, there is one difference that changes everything. Cisco's customers had almost no business of their own. Nvidia's are real companies. Open AI already brings in close to $70 billion a year from more than a billion users. And the big cloud companies throw off about $600 billion of their own cash every single year. And that is exactly what's paying for most of this buildout. So for Cambrian, Cisco's money was the entire company. But for Open AI, it's a bridge to customers who are already paying. So the circle only breaks if the real demand stops showing up. So for me, I'm watching the users, not the loop that's in the news cycle.

所以这不是一个正在减速的产业该有的曲线。因此，我们要思考这两条线的关系，一条线是利率，它决定我们愿意为未来的现金流付多少倍的估值。另一条线是这些公司实际现在就赚到的钱，他决定未来的现金流本身有多少。那现在的情况是，第一条线的确在恶化，但第二条线明显在加速，这就是我们反复讲的那个区别。 当股票出现下跌时，到底是估值的消化还是基本面的恶化？ 估值的消化，最典型的就是此前存储股所经历的大规模下跌。那这是好公司被便宜的卖掉，因为热钱暂时流走了，但基本面恶化是完全不同的情况，它是公司本身出了问题，前者是机会，后者是陷阱。所以相信很多朋友们现在手里有大量的AI股票，我们一定要区分手中的这些股票。 到底，他们现在是已经有了明显的基本面改善，还是依然处在一个炒概念的阶段？ 这将决定当这样的市场冲击来临时，他们能否经得起考验。总而言之，说了这么多数据来给朋友们说些干货，现在到底应该怎么操作？第一，我认为一定要做的就是我们的核心仓位，千万不要动。 但这个大前提是一定要，确保我们手中的股票是高质量，已经有稳定的现金流和健康的财务报表，并且估值也处在一个相对合理的水平的股票。 这一类股票才能作为核心仓位。那朋友们肯定会问，既然我们觉得大概率要跌，我先把它卖了，跌完再买回来不是更好吗？我们来算一笔账，如果我们想通过这个操作赚钱，需要连续做对两个决定，就是卖在跌之前，买在涨之前。那刚才我们说过，历史数据告诉我们，这种回撤是又深又短的。 底部很可能只有三五天。 第二点就是对核心仓位以外的股票进行适当的减仓，但减仓要按规则减，不要按情绪减。我们从来不去试图预测顶部在哪里，我们要做的就是和朋友们强调过无数次的去系统性的兑现利润。 那这个方法也很简单，我们盯住一个关键的技术位，比如标普五百这一轮的最高点是8月13日的7799，如果接下来指数反复冲这个位置，两次三次都上不去，那就是一个明显的信号，我们就可以把那些涨的最多最拥挤的仓位去进行部分的止盈。 那注意我们要做的是部分的止盈，而不是清仓。这是为了让我们手中留有部分的现金，一旦出现机会时，我们还有钱能够补进去。但如果没有出现大幅度的下跌，我们也不会完全的踏空。 第三点就是我们把购物清单写出来，提前确定下来我们想要抄底的股票，并且写上明显的价位。那这一点现在听起来或许非常简单，因为我们心情是非常平静的，可以理性的判断哪些公司值得买买在什么位置。但当市场出现大规模回调的时候。 我们心态也会出现很大的变化，所以等到那个时候再去找公司买，肯定会变得更难一些。因此现在我们写一个清单，就是给未来那个惊慌的自己准备的，而且买的时候也不要一次性的完成建仓，可以分成两到三笔。这样做的目的并不是买在最低点，而是确保我们一定能够买到相对合适的价格。 同时避免因为恐慌完全错过了这样的机会。 第四点，我们要做的就是留现金，并且不要用过度的杠杆，无论是快速的涨还是跌，在一个我们已经明知道波动会放大的窗口里加杠杆是最没有必要的风险现金在这种时候。 不是闲置，它反而是一个期权。如果风险没有发生，我们本来就有仓位在市场里，但如果风险发生了，现金就是全场最值钱的东西。那现在市场的机会到底在哪里？ 我给朋友们分享一个筛选的角度，今天的AI板块已经彻底分化了，买AI这个说法本身已经失效了当一次利率驱动的抛售来临时，它是不分青红皂白的好公司，坏公司都会一起打折，但区别就是有些跌的幅度大，有些跌的幅度小，有些之后会迅速反弹，有些永远就跌下去了。我们举几个简单的例子。 videos.transcript: AI is ending mankind—isn't the  hottest topic everyone's discussing  lately whether AI will one day cause  human civilization to disappear? Just  look at how the CEOs of Anthropic and  OpenAI recently came out saying they  think AI development should be slowed  down. According to their insight, "It  is getting out of control, bro, it is  getting scary as hell." Many people  have different views; take Trump, for  example, who feels we shouldn't let off  the gas. If we do, and we let China  overtake us, China will be the one  laughing. Even though it seemed like he  and Xi Jinping were buddy-buddy again  just the day before, regardless, this  at least shows that everyone is still  skeptical about AI's development, right ? Let me quote what I consider the  stupidest interview question I've ever  seen on CNBC; take a look. What happens  if AI doesn't succeed?  I think we have a big correction.  How big?  That's a hard question. " What happens if AI fails?""The stock  market will crash." Look, what happens  if you stub your toe on a scooter pedal ? It hurts—is there any other  possibility? What the hell is going on?  What exactly did I just watch? The  point is, at least for now, people  don't believe AI will 100%have a  positive impact or that its success  rate is 100%, right? If the success  rate isn't 100%, and you put 100%of  your portfolio into AI companies—if  you can sleep at night, then sure, no  problem. AMD, NVIDIA, and Palantir are  all great companies. But if investing  100%in AI companies is keeping you up  at night, maybe today we should think  about which companies can succeed with  or without AI. So, today I want to  share five companies that will succeed  whether AI takes us out of the galaxy  or whether AI fails and wipes out human  civilization. Hope you enjoy it. Let's  review our small agreement: if you  finish watching this video and actually  gain some value or learn something, you  might consider clicking the link for  Interactive Brokers below. I genuinely  recommend this broker; if you open an  account, I think it's the safest place  on the market to invest in US stocks.  Alright, even if you don't open an  account, clicking the link won't cost  you a single cent, but Interactive  Brokers will add a chicken leg to my  lunch for every click. So, the main  course of my lunch is in your hands,  everyone. Of course, only click if you  find it valuable after watching. If you  think this video is trash or stupid  after watching it, then by all means,  don't click anything at all. Guys,  let's get right into the video. So,  just this month, Dario Amodei published  an article called "We Must Pace the  Frontier," explaining why he thinks the  pace of AI development should be  slightly controlled, because he feels  that now...This article sparked a very  heated discussion. The next day, OpenAI  CEO Sam Altman immediately stepped up,  saying, "I agree with Dario that we  need to pace the frontier." But not  everyone shares the same sentiment as  Sam Altman or Dario. Another hero we  could mention, Donald Trump—Trump has  said "This is a hoax, that is a hoax"  at least a hundred times. Haven't heard  the word "hoax" before? It means a  trick, a prank, or something fake. On  the other hand, when Jensen Huang was  in an interview—I don't know who with , probably nobody—but anyway, he gets  a call from Trump: "Mr. President." He  puts it on speaker, and in front of the  whole world, Trump tells everyone on  this call with Jensen Huang why he  thinks—he didn't name names, but he  thinks these narratives or people  trying to hinder AI development are  basically a joke. Okay, so for this " hoax" guy, how does he view those who  suggest we should slow down AI? "For  ulterior reasons," have you seen this  phrase? Ulterior—this is a very  sophisticated, rare word. It means " having hidden motives." In other words,  he believes—though he didn't name  them—that people like Dario or Sam  Altman who think we should pace AI are  being "ulterior." Meaning they don't  really think it's dangerous or  world-ending; rather, they might be  trying to achieve some commercial gain  or political agenda, so he calls it " ulterior motives." And what about Musk?  What does the world's richest man have  to say? He believes AI is what we often  call high risk, high reward. He says, " It is worth the risk, it is worth the  risk." As LVMH is the  leader in luxury goods, its valuation  has always enjoyed a high premium;  although it has fallen by 30-40% recently, its ratio remains above 25. Anyway, this is the latest KPI  officially put forward by them, so I'm  sharing it with you all. Is there  potential undervaluation? It doesn’t mean  that if someone says it has the widest  moat you should accept it blindly, or  if they say it has no moat, you should  believe it—it doesn't work like that.  The example I want to give you is  Berkshire Hathaway. But this  company, which Buffett has been running  for over 60 years, is actually rated as  having a "narrow" moat by Morningstar —a level lower than many companies  with "wide" moats. Then this analyst  uses 2,590 words to explain why its  moat is only "narrow," while they  barely touch upon another company,  Texas Roadhouse, which is just a  restaurant. So they are desperate to  explain why they think its moat is " narrow," and these reports are actually  free, so I suggest everyone take a look . The last thing you should do is think , "Oh, Morningstar says Berkshire’s  moat is 'narrow,' so it must be worse  than Costco"—I don’t think that’s  right, because I’m not even sure if  the analyst believes what they’re  saying; otherwise, why spend so much  space explaining why you rated it as " narrow"? I don't know, man, but this is  just a heads-up: you should treat it as  a reference, not as an absolute  standard. Anyway, there’s nothing  much to say about Costco; other than it  being very expensive, there are no  issues at all. And the most impressive  thing about it is its business model.  The title here is "What the hell is  this, bro." Do you guys see this  renewal rate? In the US and Canada, the  renewal rate is 92.3%, meaning 92.3 out  of 100 people will renew their  membership next year. Folks, this is  the renewal rate, mind you. You see  software companies talk about retention  rates; anything over 90%is considered  good, but Costco is insane. This is a  renewal rate, which isn't based on  dollar amount, but on the number of  people. Why do software companies  sometimes have a 100%retention rate?  Because their unit prices go up, and  customers spend more on their software.  But the thing is, customers don't spend  more on a Costco membership card. Do  you really understand what that means?  So, which is more impressive: a 90% renewal rate or a 90%retention rate?  It’s the 90%renewal rate. I have  never seen a company—and this isn't  even a software company—where a  retail store's renewal rate outperforms  software companies. This is ridiculous,  bro. He essentially applied the  advantages of a software business to a  retail store. In the whole world,  he’s probably the only one who can  play this game, and he’s actually  pulling it off. Beyond that 90%+  renewal rate, they are steadily  expanding their business footprint  every year. For instance, in 2026, they  are confirmed to open 25 new locations,  and in 2027—well, their fiscal year  2027, as it differs from the calendar  year—they'll add 20 more, or rather,  over 25. The headline here is: "They  just don't give a damn." They don't  care about AI or anything else; they  just expand by 25 to 27 stores every  year. They are extremely consistent,  and if they have excess cash, they just  issue a one-time dividend. That's it.  So, Costco is a dream company that  every investor would want in their  portfolio. But if you look  at the three to five-year trend, the  current valuation isn't actually that  expensive. So, the headline is saying,  "In the middle of nowhere," where  you're not quite sure if the valuation  is expensive or cheap relative to its  history. Looking at the numbers,  Costco's growth rate is under 10%. I'm  saying that a 40x revenue multiple is  astronomical for a company with 10% growth, but there's no helping it—who  told them to be Costco? I have to say,  if Costco's Price-to-Free-Cash-Flow  ratio drops below 40x, I think that  would be a very, very good opportunity. Morningstar gives them a  "narrow" moat, but once again, take it  with a grain of salt. Let's first  take a look at the financial reports.  Its growth is fine; its revenue is  currently re-accelerating. The only  downside, if we ignore valuation, is  that its short-term debt is a bit high.  But restaurants have one advantage,  similar to telecom companies: they have  very stable, or should I say, very  visible cash flow coming in. As long as  people come in to eat, I have money  coming in—it's the same idea as a  subscription model, okay. So, you can  give them a bit of a pass on a poor  current ratio, as long as their  long-term debt isn't an issue. If both  aren't a mess, it looks unlikely  they’ll go under for now, okay. Of  course, you still need to pay attention , because this is still a minor red  flag. As I said earlier, it's not easy  for restaurants to have a moat, because  if you open a restaurant, I can open  one too. So what makes your moat real?  Keep in mind, don't think that a " narrow" rating is necessarily bad. " Narrow" means there is a moat; it’s  just not as obvious as others. It's  actually a pretty decent score. The  truly impressive thing about The  Cheesecake Factory is the sheer breadth  of its menu, which is almost impossible  to replicate. What I’m showing you on  the right isn't just one item; it’s  the variety. This is the list of meal  categories I pulled from their official  website—just the categories. For  everything, like the appetizers, if you  click in, there are probably 20 options . Then, for something like fish, there  are maybe 20 more. So, with over 30  categories and 20 items in each, they  have at least several hundred dishes.  Because they have one of the largest  menus in America—it's even been the  subject of research, with headlines  like "The Cheesecake Factory runs one  of America's biggest menus"—how do  they manage to control so many items  and maintain such consistent quality?  Since this has been studied  academically, it’s clear that what  makes this restaurant difficult to  replicate is the vastness of its menu.  If you wanted to copy a vegan fried  chicken restaurant, that’s relatively  easy—you just need to know how to fry  chicken. But is replicating The  Cheesecake Factory’s business model  that simple? No. It’s not just about  having the ingredients ready; your  management needs to be far superior to  everyone else’s, not just a little  better, to pull off what they do. So,  why has their stock performed so well  this year? Let’s take a look at their  margins, specifically the operating  margin. Back in 2023, or three years  ago, it was around 2%. Now, it has  steadily climbed to 6%and is still  rising, as their net income margin is  currently just under 5%but is expected  to exceed 5.4%this year. So, with growth  re-accelerating and margins expanding,  Cheesecake Factory is trending in a  very positive direction. That’s why  the stock price is so strong today, but  is it actually worth its current  valuation of around 25 times earnings?  If you look at the 15-to 20-year  average, the current valuation isn't  actually that expensive, so you could  argue it deserves its 25x multiple. So, you can't definitively say whether  the valuation is cheap or expensive.  Anyway, if you look at its history,  it's okay, but just looking at the 25x  figure, it’s not really that cheap,  especially since it's a restaurant, and  a restaurant with single-digit growth,  okay. Come on, guys,  let’s look at Ferrari's financial  reports; they are outstanding, with  growth and cash flow. This debt profile  is something you won't see at any other  car company—a perfectly balanced debt  ratio. Its only problem, like Costco,  is that it's very expensive. Can't help  it, it is named Ferrari, not GM, right?  Here, I want to help everyone  understand the difference between  luxury goods and consumer goods; the  biggest difference is depreciation. If  I go buy a Mercedes today, do you  consider it a luxury good? Well, I  don't know, but let's take a look at  how it depreciates, shall we? This  Mercedes-Benz GLE 450 had a new car  price of about 3.8 million NTD back in  2019. Now, checking the Mercedes-Benz  certified pre-owned website, this 2019  car, after seven years, has depreciated  to 1.48 million, which is about right.  Because we all know car prices usually  get cut after four years, and since  this one is already seven years old,  1.48 million is typical for a Mercedes.  Although Taiwanese people love driving  them and say rich people drive Mercedes —and yes, buying one does show you  have some financial means—it doesn't  make it a "luxury good," because luxury  goods don't depreciate like that.  Let’s look at how Ferrari depreciates , shall we? Why did I choose a 2019  Mercedes for comparison? Because I  found this same car on Ferrari’s  certified pre-owned website: a 2019 488  Pista Spider. Back in 2019, the new car  price was 22 million. Of course, if you  added some wild options, it could go up  to 25 million or more. This is exactly what I mean by  the difference between a luxury good  and a consumable; it’s not that  luxury goods don’t depreciate. In  fact, they often gain value over time,  like wine or an Hermès bag. Don't  think that just because you bought it,  it's used up; a pre-owned Hermès bag  is sometimes more expensive than a  brand-new one. So, why would you think  Ferrari is in the automotive industry?  They are definitely in the luxury goods  business, right? Otherwise, look at how  ridiculous the comparison is. Comparing these two  charts shows you that Ferrari doesn't  just make cars; they make luxury goods,  okay? And you don’t just see this in  their used car market. Whether you look at Tesla, Japanese  automakers, Volkswagen, European brands , or American GM, all of them combined  might not even match that. What is this ? Let’s just look at the Return on  Equity, or ROE. ROE is at 45%. Do all  these others even add up to half of  that? So, the headline is: what? These  financial metrics can’t be explained  by traditional auto standards. A Return  on Assets of 17%, and then these other  four. These aren't just any small  players; they are the biggest names in  Japan, the U.S., and Europe, yet even  combined, they don't reach half of  Ferrari's figures. So you can  understand that holding Ferrari stock  versus holding GM stock—the  investment logic is completely  different. And because it's Ferrari... The stock has never been cheap. It’s  currently trading at nearly 50 times  valuation. Now, a 50x valuation might  look exaggerated, but why is it that  for the past three, five, or ten years,  the average price-to-free-cash-flow  ratio has been 60x? Like what the hell  is going on? Regardless,  Alphabet is a company that will thrive  perfectly fine, whether it's AI or not.  The last company is Mastercard.  Mastercard's stock price hasn't really  done anything over the past year, and  its market cap is currently around 500  billion, so it's a very large company.  Why do I like this company? If you haven't  seen it before, you're looking at it  now; its margins rival those of  software companies. The point is, while  Mastercard isn't a bank, and it isn't a  software company either, why is it a  dream business model? Because it  specializes in collecting tolls; if you  use the Mastercard network, right? Then  I take a cut from you, and another cut  from you. You don't have to do anything ; you just act as a toll collector.  It's that great. So, if you look at  these financial metrics, you see Nvidia  next to it, and the king of SaaS,  ServiceNow. This is why I say some  companies just inherently have better  business models. In the last Grab video , I mentioned that although I am a Grab  shareholder, we have to admit that  regardless of whether their management  is excellent or poor, their business  model is inherently far behind  Mastercard's. It’s a tougher road,  and the barrier to entry for others in  that market is just much lower. We have  to recognize these facts. So,  Mastercard, on the other hand, is a  dream company—in the eyes of  investors, a dream company. Compared to  Visa, while Mastercard might be number  two in terms of cash flow volume, its  real strength lies in its value-added  services; for example, you process a  payment, but you can also leverage  things like AI. So, I have to admit,  among these five companies today,  Mastercard is more likely to be  impacted by AI—whether for better or  worse, I don't know, but it’s more  susceptible. As AI becomes more  advanced, it can help Mastercard with  cybersecurity and fraud prevention. For  instance, if you make a purchase and  Mastercard detects it might be  fraudulent, they can block it. These  value-added services account for over  40%of their total revenue, so their  growth potential is actually better  than Visa’s. That’s how it is.  Because in terms of what I just  mentioned—cybersecurity—they are  ahead of Visa. Visa’s main revenue  source still relies on the payment  network I mentioned earlier, basically  just collecting those "protection fees, " if you will. Looking at the stock  price, it’s currently at 31 times  price-to-cash flow; the P/E ratio is  pretty much the same. Compared to its  10-year, 15-year, or 5-year average, it  looks quite reasonable, as it has been  over 35 times in the past. Even though  its overall growth rate has slowed down  significantly, the growth rate of its  value-added services segment, at 20%,  is still a very excellent number. So,  if you want to sleep soundly at night,  I’ve shared these five companies with  you today. No, I’m not telling you to  buy them right now, but at least  you’ve heard these names. Then, based  on your own experience—for example, I  use Mastercard, but I might not use  Visa, or I’ve never owned a Ferrari —you might prioritize companies  you’ve actually used. So, it really  depends on your personal user  experience or your investment style  when deciding which company to buy. Anyway, I’m just  sharing these five companies that I  think are less likely to be negatively  impacted by AI for you to get to know.  Alright, everyone, those are the five  companies that I believe will do well  regardless of whether AI succeeds or  not. videos.transcript: Hello 大家好我是 Terry 今天要跟大家分享一個很開心的事情 沒錯就像影片標題寫的一樣 我發行了一張信用卡 好啦其實也不算是 完全是我自己發行的啦 應該說是聯名卡 但是至少呢這整張卡的設計 還有它背後的故事呢 是關於這個 YouTube 頻道 我覺得也算是這個 YouTube 頻道 成立了六年 對沒錯已經六年了 完成了一個里程碑那我覺得真的很酷 所以想把這個故事分享給大家 其實這個頻道從開始到現在呢 我並沒有把它當成是 一個專門講某一個主題的頻道 這個頻道一直以來呢就是在分享 關於我自己正在做的事情 等於說基本上就是 把我過去六年的人生 放在網路上面給大家看 沒有什麼任何的 filter 也沒有人設 從最開始我們講 這個矽谷工程師的薪水 然後分享我自己個人投資理財的 一些經驗跟心得 生活中的一些大小事啊 買了房子修了水管旅居的生活
